To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel scheme to predict atomic forces as a vector quantity, rather than sets a scalar components, by machine learning with covariants kernels.

(i) we introduce a new class of kernels that are covariant under rotation, which is essential for the correct treatment of atomic forces as vectorial quantities; (ii) we show how the new kernels can be used to predict forces with high accuracy in a variety of materials, including defective systems; and (iii) we show that the new kernels can often be expressed as a sum of pair interactions, which allows for efficient implementation in classical molecular dynamics simulations

we propose a novel scheme to predict atomic forces as vectors via Gaussian process regression with a kernel function that is covariant with the target configuration, and we show that such covariances can be obtained by integrating over the elements of an appropriate point group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel scheme to learn accurate atomic forces by GP regression with matrix-valued kernels.
the design and application of machine learning (ML) methods in materials science.
the development of a machine learning framework to predict atomic forces as vectors, and to provide accurate interatomic potentials for a variety of systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our covariant kernel is an excellent tool to accurately predict forces in real systems.
the covariant kernel approach, when applied to a sufficiently large training set, is able to provide accurate predictions of atomic forces, and thus of atomic positions and energies.

the covariant kernels, in particular the ones that are analytically integrable, can be used to predict forces with a very high accuracy and that the accuracy of the predictions is very close to that obtained by the conventional scalar kernel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel scheme for predicting accurate interatomic forces by GP regression with matrix-valued kernels.
our approach can be viewed as the covariant generalisation of the Gaussian approximation potential method.
the covariant kernels provide an accurate representation of atomic forces in a variety of systems and that they are computationally efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by using a covariant GP regression scheme, one can achieve an accurate prediction of the forces acting on atoms in a material without having to resort to the more expensive and computationally demanding prediction of the energy.
covariant GP regression is an accurate and computationally efficient approach for learning interatomic force fields.

covariant kernels can be used to obtain accurate interatomic force fields for a wide range of materials and defects, and can be applied to other problems where vectorial quantities need to be predicted.
